answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil floods by charging a costly inlet to identity: before an account may submit work, it must lock a bond held behind a slow release queue and slashed if peers catch it faking. One operator with a thousand keys then pays a thousand deposits plus the yield forgone on each, and the delay stops capital cycling across fresh wallets; attested history cannot be copied, so new keys start at zero weight. Fresh wallets also cannot siphon the easy nectar of rewards without paying what real agents pay, and the pigment of identical bonds is easy to freeze.
